question: What identity guarantee, trust anchor, and outbound request paths should OpenClaw officially support for agent attestation?
rationale: Implementation cannot safely choose whether OpenClaw is merely self-identifying, vouching for a configured installation, or claiming hardware- or platform-backed execution; each choice has materially different privacy, spoofing, key-management, and ownership consequences.

options.title: Scoped self-identification
options.body: Expose opt-in, audience-scoped metadata through a generic plugin or runtime seam while explicitly documenting that it is not proof that a request was autonomous or human-free.

options.title: Platform-backed attestation
options.body: Design a verifier protocol around a hardware, hosted, or third-party trust anchor with key lifecycle, replay protection, privacy, and covered-path guarantees before adding headers.

options.title: No general core contract
options.body: Keep provider-specific attribution only and require agent-only services to use their own authenticated plugin, API-key, OAuth, wallet, or trusted-execution integration.

recommendation.title: Scoped self-identification
recommendation.body: Expose opt-in, audience-scoped metadata through a generic plugin or runtime seam while explicitly documenting that it is not proof that a request was autonomous or human-free.

likelyOwner.reason: He supplied the existing keep-open product and security direction and integrated the adjacent provider-attribution boundary.
